newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps up slightly.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps up slightly.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in quiet late trading on Friday as swap rates were seen edging up slightly, dealers said.
They said volume remained thin as players continued to stay on the sidelines with the focus mainly on liquidity.
Overnight money rose to 17 percent in the afternoon.
One European bank dealer said swap rates tended to move to the right following a tighter rupiah market.
"I have the feeling people are still short in the swap market. They did some buy back to cover positions," he said.
The dealer said this could also be due to the month-end factor as operators wanted to book their profits.
Dealers said the market was generally quiet due to a lack of fresh leads and also slow regional markets.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,342.50/42.75 in late afternoon, compared with an opening of 2,342.5/43.0.
One U.S. bank dealer said earlier the relatively tight rupiah supply in the morning caused operators to unload today dollars and this had also dragged spot dollars down slightly.
However, dealers said operators were hesitant to unload further because of the central bank's floor rate for dollars.
One said there was also no good reason to buy dollars as the domestic political tension had calmed down and the interest rate differentials remained attractive for the rupiah.
Overnight swap was at 2.7/2.8 and spot/next at 0.53/0.55.
One-month swap was at 16.50/17.25, two at 35.0/36.0, three at 52.0/52.5 and six at 103.5/104.5 points.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,340/2,458 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,340/2,386 on Friday.
